enDefinition: properly, self (but generally used to point out more definitely the object of a verb or preposition, even or namely)
Jehovah, Jewish national name of God
above, over, upon, or against (yet always in this last relation with a downward aspect) in a great variety of applications
near, with or among; often in general, to
properly, the whole; hence, all, any or every (in the singular only, but often in a plural sense)
not (the simple or abs. negation); by implication, no; often used with other particles
who, which, what, that; also (as an adverb and a conjunction) when, where, how, because, in order that, etc.
a son (as a builder of the family name), in the widest sense (of literal and figurative relationship, including grandson, subject, nation, quality or condition, etc., (like father or brother), etc.)
(by implication) very widely used as a relative conjunction or adverb (as below); often largely modified by other particles annexed
to exist, i.e. be or become, come to pass (always emphatic, and not a mere copula or auxiliary)
to do or make, in the broadest sense and widest application

gods in the ordinary sense; but specifically used (in the plural thus, especially with the article) of the supreme God; occasionally applied by way of deference to magistrates; and sometimes as a superlative
to go or come (in a wide variety of applications)
Jisrael, a symbolical name of Jacob; also (typically) of his posterity
the earth (at large, or partitively a land)
a day (as the warm hours), whether literal (from sunrise to sunset, or from one sunset to the next), or figurative (a space of time defined by an associated term), (often used adverb)
a man as an individual or a male person; often used as an adjunct to a more definite term (and in such cases frequently not expressed in translation)
the face (as the part that turns); used in a great variety of applications (literally and figuratively); also (with prepositional prefix) as a preposition (before, etc.)
a house (in the greatest variation of applications, especially family, etc.)
to give, used with greatest latitude of application (put, make, etc.)

he (she or it); only expressed when emphatic or without a verb; also (intensively) self, or (especially with the article) the same; sometimes (as demonstrative) this or that; occasionally (instead of copula) as or are
a people (as a congregated unit); specifically, a tribe (as those of Israel); hence (collectively) troops or attendants; figuratively, a flock
a hand (the open one (indicating power, means, direction, etc.),
a word; by implication, a matter (as spoken of) or thing; adverbially, a cause
to see, literally or figuratively (in numerous applications, direct and implied, transitive, intransitive and causative)
as far (or long, or much) as, whether of space (even unto) or time (during, while, until) or degree (equally with)
properly, a part of; hence (prepositionally), from or out of in many senses
father, in a literal and immediate, or figurative and remote application
the masculine demonstrative pronoun, this or that
to hear intelligently (often with implication of attention, obedience, etc.; causatively, to tell, etc.)
perhaps properly, to arrange; but used figuratively (of words), to speak; rarely (in a destructive sense) to subdue
a city (a place guarded by waking or a watch) in the widest sense (even of a mere encampment or post)
properly, to sit down (specifically as judge. in ambush, in quiet); by implication, to dwell, to remain; causatively, to settle, to marry
to go (causatively, bring) out, in a great variety of applications, literally and figuratively, direct and proxim.
David, the youngest son of Jesse
to turn back (hence, away) transitively or intransitively, literally or figuratively (not necessarily with the idea of return to the starting point); generally to retreat; often adverbial, again
used very widely as demonstrative, lo!; interrogative, whether?; or conditional, if, although; also Oh that!, when; hence, as a negative, not
adverb or preposition, with (i.e. in conjunction with), in varied applications; specifically, equally with; often with prepositional prefix (and then usually unrepresented in English)
to walk (literally or figuratively); causatively, to carry (in various senses)
properly, united, i.e. one; or (as an ordinal) first
to take (in the widest variety of applications)

to know (properly, to ascertain by seeing); used in a great variety of senses, figuratively, literally, euphemistically and inferentially (including observation, care, recognition; and causatively, instruction, designation, punishment, etc.)
an eye (literally or figuratively); by analogy, a fountain (as the eye of the landscape)
to ascend, intransitively (be high) or actively (mount); used in a great variety of senses, primary and secondary, literal and figurative
properly, nearness (used only as a preposition or an adverb), near; hence, generally, with, by, at, among, etc.
a year (as a revolution of time)
an appellation, as amark or memorial of individuality; by implication honor, authority, character
to send away, for, or out (in a great variety of applications)
to die (literally or figuratively); causatively, to kill
there (transferring to time) then; often thither, or thence
Jehudah (or Judah), the name of five Israelites; also of the tribe descended from the first, and of its territory
thou and thee, or (plural) ye and you
a non-entity; generally used as a negative particle
properly, set upright; hence (figuratively as adjective) just; but usually (as adverb or conjunction) rightly or so (in various applications to manner, time and relation; often with other particles)
properly, assemblage; used only adverbially also, even, yea, though; often repeated as correl. both...and
properly, a breathing creature, i.e. animal of (abstractly) vitality; used very widely in a literal, accommodated or figurative sense (bodily or mental)

properly, interrogative what? (including how? why? when?); but also exclamation, what! (including how!), or indefinitely what (including whatever, and even relatively, that which); often used with prefixes in various adverbial or conjunctive senses
literally one officiating, a priest; also (by courtesy) an acting priest (although a layman)
to call out to (i.e. properly, address by name, but used in a wide variety of applications)
not (the qualified negation, used as a deprecative); once (Job 24:25) as a noun, nothing
properly, the hind part; generally used as an adverb or conjunction, after (in various senses)
a road (as trodden); figuratively, a course of life or mode of action, often adverb
bad or (as noun) evil (natural or moral)
to lift, in a great variety of applications, literal and figurative, absolute and relative
Jerushalaim or Jerushalem, the capital city of Palestine
Mitsrajim, i.e. Upper and Lower Egypt
a brother (used in the widest sense of literal relationship and metaphorical affinity or resemblance (like father))
to rise (in various applications, literal, figurative, intensive and causative)
the head (as most easily shaken), whether literal or figurative (in many applications, of place, time, rank, itc.)
the heart; also used (figuratively) very widely for the feelings, the will and even the intellect; likewise for the centre of anything
a daughter (used in the same wide sense as other terms of relationship, literally and figuratively)
to put (used in a great variety of applications, literal, figurative, inferentially, and elliptically)
a hundred; also as a multiplicative and a fraction
water; figuratively, juice; by euphemism, urine, semen
properly, like this, i.e. by implication, (of manner) thus (or so); also (of place) here (or hither); or (of time) now
a foreign nation; hence, a Gentile; also (figuratively) a troop of animals, or a flight of locusts

good (as an adjective) in the widest sense; used likewise as a noun, both in the masculine and the feminine, the singular and the plural (good, a good or good thing, a good man or woman; the good, goods or good things, good men or women), also as an adverb (well)
to cross over; used very widely of any transition (literal or figurative; transitive, intransitive, intensive, causative); specifically, to cover (in copulation)
ruddy i.e. a human being (an individual or the species, mankind, etc.)
a mountain or range of hills (sometimes used figuratively)
great (in any sense); hence, older; also insolent
to stand, in various relations (literal and figurative, intransitive and transitive)
the bottom (as depressed); only adverbially, below (often with prepositional prefix underneath), in lieu of, etc.
to walk (in a great variety of applications, literally and figuratively)
hence (the ox's head being the first letter of the alphabet, and this eventually used as a numeral) a thousand
to strike (lightly or severely, literally or figuratively)
to bear young; causatively, to beget; medically, to act as midwife; specifically, to show lineage
the mouth (as the means of blowing), whether literal or figurative (particularly speech); specifically edge, portion or side; adverbially (with preposition) according to
properly, iteration or continuance; used only adverbially (with or without preposition), again, repeatedly, still, more
a mass of persons (or figuratively, things), especially reg. organized forwar (an army); by implication, a campaign, literally or figuratively (specifically, hardship, worship)
properly, to hedge about (as with thorns), i.e. guard; generally, to protect, attend to, etc.
a sacred place or thing; rarely abstract, sanctity
abundant (in quantity, size, age, number, rank, quality)
properly, to come forth to, i.e. appear or exist; transitively, to attain, i.e. find or acquire; figuratively, to occur, meet or be present
the Lord (used as a proper name of God only)
properly, concealed, i.e. the vanishing point; generally, time out of mind (past or future), i.e. (practically) eternity; frequentatively, adverbial (especially with prepositional prefix) always
to fall, in a great variety of applications (intransitive or causative, literal or figurative)
at this time, whether adverb, conjunction or expletive

properly, a verdict (favorable or unfavorable) pronounced judicially, especially a sentence or formal decree (human or (participant's) divine law, individual or collective), including the act, the place, the suit, the crime, and the penalty; abstractly, justice, including a participant's right or privilege (statutory or customary), or even a style
who? (occasionally, by a peculiar idiom, of things); also (indefinitely) whoever; often used in oblique construction with prefix or suffix
a head person (of any rank or class)
the sky (as aloft; the dual perhaps alluding to the visible arch in which the clouds move, as well as to the higher ether where the celestial bodies revolve)
a bisection, i.e. (by implication) the centre
drought; also a cutting instrument (from its destructive effect), as a knife, sword, or other sharp implement
between (repeated before each noun, often with other particles); also as a conjunction, either...or
Shaul, the name of an Edomite and two Israelites
silver (from its pale color); by implication, money
'I pray', 'now', or 'then'; added mostly to verbs (in the Imperative or Future), or to interjections, occasionally to an adverb or conjunction
properly, a standing, i.e. a spot; but used widely of a locality (general or specific); also (figuratively) of a condition (of body or mind)

a sea (as breaking in noisy surf) or large body of water; specifically (with the article), the Mediterranean Sea; sometimes a large river, or an artifical basin; locally, the west, or (rarely) the south
seven (as the sacred full one); also (adverbially) seven times; by implication, a week; by extension, an indefinite number
gold, figuratively, something gold-colored (i.e. yellow), as oil, a clear sky

to descend (literally, to go downwards; or conventionally to a lower region, as the shore, a boundary, the enemy, etc.; or figuratively, to fall); causatively, to bring down (in all the above applications)

wind; by resemblance breath, i.e. a sensible (or even violent) exhalation; figuratively, life, anger, unsubstantiality; by extension, a region of the sky; by resemblance spirit, but only of a rational being (including its expression and functions)
an opening, i.e. door or gate

properly, to front, i.e. stand boldly out opposite; by implication (causatively), to manifest; figuratively, to announce (always by word of mouth to one present); specifically, to expose, predict, explain, praise
blood (as that which when shed causes death) of man or an animal; by analogy, the juice of the grape; figuratively (especially in the plural) bloodshed (i.e. drops of blood)
alive; hence, raw (flesh); fresh (plant, water, year), strong; also (as noun, especially in the feminine singular and masculine plural) life (or living thing), whether literally or figuratively
to reign; inceptively, to ascend the throne; causatively, to induct into royalty; hence (by implication) to take counsel
a tent (as clearly conspicuous from a distance)
that, used as relative conjunction, and especially (with a preposition) in adverbial phrases; also as preposition of
(as noun) a circle, neighbour, or environs; but chiefly (as adverb, with or without preposition) around
to kneel; by implication to bless God (as an act of adoration), and (vice-versa) man (as a benefit); also (by euphemism) to curse (God or the king, as treason)
a tree (from its firmness); hence, wood (plural sticks)
to fear; morally, to revere; caus. to frighten
properly, to eye or (generally) to heed, i.e. pay attention; by implication, to respond; by extension to begin to speak; specifically to sing, shout, testify, announce
something prepared, i.e. any apparatus (as an implement, utensil, dress, vessel or weapon)
desire (and so probably in Proverbs 31:4); hence (by way of alternative) or, also if
a battle (i.e. the engagement); generally, war (i.e. warfare)
a family, i.e. circle of relatives; figuratively, a class (of persons), a species (of animals) or sort (of things); by extension a tribe or people
to visit (with friendly or hostile intent); by analogy, to oversee, muster, charge, care for, miss, deposit, etc.
properly, vehemence, i.e. (with or without preposition) vehemently; by implication, wholly, speedily, etc. (often with other words as an intensive or superlative; especially when repeated)
food (for man or beast), especially bread, or grain (for making it)
an offence (sometimes habitual sinfulness), and its penalty, occasion, sacrifice, or expiation; also (concretely) an offender
time, especially (adverb with preposition) now, when, etc.
a Pelishtite or inhabitant of Pelesheth
to fasten upon; hence, to seize, be strong (figuratively, courageous, causatively strengthen, cure, help, repair, fortify), obstinate; to bind, restrain, conquer
to cut (off, down or asunder); by implication, to destroy or consume; specifically, to covenant (i.e. make an alliance or bargain, originally by cutting flesh and passing between the pieces)
a step or (collectively, stairs, as ascending); usually a holocaust (as going up in smoke)
to work (in any sense); by implication, to serve, till, (causatively) enslave, etc.
a Levite or descendant of Levi
a compact (because made by passing between pieces of flesh)
the new moon; by implication, a month
to approach (causatively, bring near) for whatever purpose
properly, the nose or nostril; hence, the face, and occasionally a person; also (from the rapid breathing in passion) ire
a collective name for a flock (of sheep or goats); also figuratively (of men)
properly, heed, i.e. purpose; used only adverbially, on account of (as a motive or an aim), teleologically, in order that
a pasture (i.e. open field, whither cattle are driven); by implication, a desert; also speech (including its organs)
flesh (from its freshness); by extension, body, person; also (by euphemistically) the pudenda of aman
Paroh, a general title of Egyptian kings
to live, whether literally or figuratively; causatively, to revive
morally wrong; concretely, an (actively) bad person
Babel (i.e. Babylon), including Babylonia and the Babylonian empire
the heart (as the most interior organ);

a branch (as extending); figuratively, a tribe; also a rod, whether for chastising (figuratively, correction), ruling (a sceptre), throwing (a lance), or walking (a staff; figuratively, a support of life, e.g. bread)
kindness; by implication (towards God) piety; rarely (by opposition) reproof, or (subject.) beauty
a foot (as used in walking); by implication, a step; by euphemistically the pudenda
to fill or (intransitively) be full of, in a wide application (literally and figuratively)
properly, a mother (i.e. unit of measure, or the fore-arm (below the elbow), i.e. a cubit; also a door-base (as a bond of the entrance)
strength; as adjective, mighty; especially the Almighty (but used also of any deity)
properly, a cord (as twisted), i.e. (by implication) a boundary; by extension the territory inclosed
properly, to miss; hence (figuratively and generally) to sin; by inference, to forfeit, lack, expiate, repent, (causatively) lead astray, condemn
(concretely) a boy (as active), from the age of infancy to adolescence; by implication, a servant; also (by interch. of sex), a girl (of similar latitude in age)
safe, i.e. (figuratively) well, happy, friendly; also (abstractly) welfare, i.e. health, prosperity, peace
properly, to mark (so as to be recognized), i.e. to remember; by implication, to mention;  to be male
properly, a twist (away of the light), i.e. night; figuratively, adversity
an action (good or bad); generally, a transaction; abstractly, activity; by implication, a product (specifically, a poem) or (generally) property
probably a force, whether of men, means or other resources; an army, wealth, virtue, valor, strength
to occupy (by driving out previous tenants, and possessing in their place); by implication, to seize, to rob, to inherit; also to expel, to impoverish, to ruin
seed; figuratively, fruit, plant, sowing-time, posterity
to grave, by implication, to write (describe, inscribe, prescribe, subscribe)
properly, the nearest part, i.e. the center, whether literal, figurative or adverbial (especially with preposition)
to search out (by any method, specifically in worship or prayer); by implication, to strive after

properly, an appointment, i.e. a fixed time or season; specifically, a festival; conventionally ayear; by implication, an assembly (as convened for a definite purpose); technically the congregation; by extension, the place of meeting; also a signal (as appointed beforehand)
properly, something inherited, i.e. (abstractly) occupancy, or (concretely) an heirloom; generally an estate, patrimony or portion
a precept or statute, especially the Decalogue or Pentateuch
a mother (as the bond of the family); in a wide sense (both literally and figuratively (like father))

properly, to be erect (i.e. stand perpendicular); hence (causatively) to set up, in a great variety of applications, whether literal (establish, fix, prepare, apply), or figurative (appoint, render sure, proper or prosperous)
a covering, i.e. clothing; also treachery or pillage
an encampment (of travellers or troops); hence, an army, whether literal (of soldiers) or figurative (of dancers, angels, cattle, locusts, stars; or even the sacred courts)
to stretch or spread out; by implication, to bend away (including moral deflection); used in a great variety of application
to loosen, i.e. relinquish, permit, etc.
six (as an overplus  beyond five or the fingers of the hand); as ord. sixth
properly, dawn (as the break of day); generally, morning
to snatch away, whether in a good or a bad sense
a messenger; specifically, of God, i.e. an angel (also a prophet, priest or teacher)
Joseph, the name of seven Israelites
to lie down (for rest, sexual connection, decease or any other purpose)
a donation; euphemistically, tribute; specifically a sacrificial offering (usually bloodless and voluntary)
to have affection for (sexually or otherwise)
to add or augment (often adverbial, to continue to do a thing)
properly, to be open, wide or free, i.e. (by implication) to be safe; causatively, to free or succor
to end, whether intransitive (to cease, be finished, perish) or transitived (to complete, prepare, consume)
to judge, i.e. pronounce sentence (for or against); by implication, to vindicate or punish; by extenssion, to govern; passively, to litigate (literally or figuratively)
to gather for any purpose; hence, to receive, take away, i.e. remove (destroy, leave behind, put up, restore, etc.)
properly, separation; by implication, a part of the body, branch of atree, bar forcarrying; figuratively, chief of a city; especially (with prepositional prefix) as an adverb, apart, only, besides
properly, weight, but only figuratively in a good sense, splendor or copiousness
the hollow hand or palm (so of the paw of an animal, of the sole, and even of the bowl of a dish or sling, the handle of a bolt, the leaves of a palm-tree); figuratively, power
to be able, literally (can, could) or morally (may, might)
grease, especially liquid (as from the olive, often perfumed); figuratively, richness
to be high actively, to rise or raise (in various applications, literally or figuratively)
properly, strength; hence, anything strong; specifically a chief (politically); also a ram (from his strength); a pilaster (as a strong support); an oak or other strong tree
a scion, i.e. (literally) a stick (for punishing, writing, fighting, ruling, walking, etc.) or (figuratively) a clan
a yard (as inclosed by a fence); also a hamlet (as similarly surrounded with walls)
properly, a dumb beast; especially any large quadruped or animal (often collective)
broadness. i.e. (concrete) the ear (from its form in man)
properly, writing (the art or a document); by implication, a book
to denude (especially in a disgraceful sense); by implication, to exile (captives being usually stripped); figuratively, to reveal
to seven oneself, i.e. swear (as if by repeating a declaration seven times)
properly, to wander away, i.e. lose oneself; by implication to perish (causative, destroy)
a command, whether human or divine (collectively, the Law)
Jarden, the principal river of Palestine
beef cattle or an animal of the ox family of either gender (as used for plowing); collectively, a herd
first, in place, time or rank (as adjective or noun)
Moab, an incestuous son of Lot; also his territory and descendants
Ephrajim, a son of Joseph; also the tribe descended from him, and its territory
to feed on; figuratively, to consume; by implication, to battle (as destruction)
ten (as an accumulation to the extent of the digits)
the lip (as a natural boundary); by implication, language; by analogy, a margin (of a vessel, water, cloth, etc.)
to inquire; by implication, to request; by extension, to demand
Abraham, the later name of Abram
to depress, i.e. prostrate (especially reflexive, in homage to royalty or God)
to be (causatively, make, pronounce or observe as) clean (ceremonially or morally)
to separate mentally (or distinguish), i.e.(generally) understand
properly, to try, i.e. (by implication) select
properly, a revolution of time, i.e. an age or generation; also a dwelling
Binjamin, youngest son of Jacob; also the tribe descended from him, and its territory
properly, deputyship, i.e. ministry; generally, employment (never servile) or work (abstractly or concretely); also property (as the result of labor)
properly, hinder; generally, next, other, etc.
properly, to tread or frequent; usually to follow (for pursuit or search); by implication, to seek or ask; specifically to worship
to be clear (orig. of sound, but usually of color); to shine; hence, to make ashow, to boast; and thus to be (clamorously) foolish; to rave; causatively, to celebrate; also to stultify
an opening (literally), i.e. door (gate) or entrance way
properly, separate by awall, i.e. outside, outdoors
to tend a flock; i.e. pasture it; intransitively, to graze (literally or figuratively); generally to rule; by extension, to associate with (as a friend)
properly, a slaughter, i.e. the flesh of an animal; by implication, a sacrifice (the victim or the act)
to be foul, especially in a ceremial or moral sense (contaminated)
to flit, i.e. vanish away (subside, escape; causatively, chase, impel, deliver)
properly, to score with a mark as a tally or record, i.e. (by implication) to inscribe, and also to enumerate; intensively, to recount, i.e. celebrate
a particle of affirmation, surely; hence (by limitation) only
rightness (abstractly), subjectively (rectitude), objectively (justice), morally (virtue) or figuratively (prosperity)
to revolve, surround, or border; used in various applications, literally and figuratively
probably to brighten up, i.e. (figuratively) be (causatively, make) blithe or gleesome
death (natural or violent); concretely, the dead, their place or state (hades); figuratively, pestilence, ruin
properly, double, i.e. second; also adverbially, again
Tsijon (as a permanent capital), a mountain of Jerusalem
properly, to plump, i.e. fill up hollows; by implication, to cover (for clothing or secrecy)
properly, hidden, i.e. dark; used only of the north as aquarter (gloomy and unknown)
Ashshur, the second son of Shem; also his descendants and the country occupied by them (i.e. Assyria), its region and its empire

properly, to touch, i.e. lay the hand upon (for any purpose; euphemistically, to lie with a woman); by implication, to reach (figuratively, to arrive, acquire); violently, to strike (punish, defeat, destroy, etc.)
a front, i.e. part opposite; specifically a counterpart, or mate; usually (adverbial, especially with preposition) over against or before
a stated assemblage (specifically, a concourse, or generally, a family or crowd)
Jirmejah, the name of eight or nine Israelites
to decay, i.e. (causatively) ruin (literally or figuratively)
Menashsheh, a grandson of Jacob, also the tribe descended from him, and its territory
properly, to pull up, especially the tent-pins, i.e. start on ajourney
Joab, the name of three Israelites
to open wide (literally or figuratively); specifically, to loosen, begin, plough, carve
to run after (usually with hostile intent; figuratively (of time) gone by)
properly, to bore, i.e. (by implication) to wound, to dissolve; figuratively, to profane (a person, place or thing), to break (one's word), to begin (as if by an 'opening wedge'); to play (the flute)
properly, to incline; by implication, to decline (of the slanting rays of evening); specifically, to pitch atent; gen. to encamp (for abode or siege)
a form of the prefix 'k-', but used separately  as, thus, so
at that time or place; also as a conjunction, therefore
a stream, especially a winter torrent; (by implication) a (narrow) valley (in which a brook runs); also a shaft (of a mine)
the right hand or side (leg, eye) of a person or other object (as the stronger and more dexterous); locally, the south
a horse (as leaping); also a swallow (from its rapid flight)
Shemuel, the name of three Israelites
properly, the upper part, used only adverbially with prefix upward, above, overhead, from the top, etc.
copper, hence, something made of that metal, i.e. coin, a fetter; figuratively, base (as compared with gold or silver)
a residence (including a shepherd's hut, the lair of animals, figuratively, the grave; also the Temple); specifically, the Tabernacle (properly, its wooden walls)
there is or are (or any other form of the verb to be, as may suit the connection)
properly, covered, i.e. a throne (as canopied)
to turn; by implication, to face, i.e. appear, look, etc.
Gilad, a region East of the Jordan; also the name of three Israelites
a number, definite (arithmetical) or indefinite (large, innumerable; small, a few); also (abstractly) narration
to slaughter an animal (usually in sacrifice)
meaning accession (used as an adverb or conjunction); also or yea; adversatively though
properly, an exalted one, i.e. a king or sheik; also a rising mist
the sun; by implication, the east; figuratively, a ray, i.e. (architectural) a notched battlement
Aram or Syria, and its inhabitants; also the name of the son of Shem, a grandson of Nahor, and of an Israelite
properly, removal; used only (in the construction) adverb as conjunction, lest
properly, to swell up, i.e. be (causatively, make) redundant
a bullock (apparently as breaking forth in wild strength, or perhaps as dividing the hoof)
Chizkijah, a king of Judah, also the name of two other Israelites
to reside or permanently stay (literally or figuratively)
an enactment; hence, an appointment (of time, space, quantity, labor or usage)
vigor, literally (force, in a good or a bad sense) or figuratively (capacity, means, produce); also (from its hardiness) a large lizard
a bone (as strong); by extension, the body; figuratively, the substance, i.e. (as pron.) selfsame

to be or come (causatively, bring) near (for any purpose); euphemistically, to lie with a woman; as an enemy, to attack; religious to worship; causatively, to present; figuratively, to adduce an argument; by reversal, to stand back
to throw out, down or away (literally or figuratively)

properly, to plait or interpenetrate, i.e. (literally) to weave or (generally) to fabricate; figuratively, to plot or contrive (usually in a malicious sense); hence (from the mental effort) to think, regard, value, compute
heat; figuratively, anger, poison (from its fever)
to catch (in a net, trap or pit); generally, to capture or occupy; also to choose (by lot); figuratively, to cohere
illumination or (concrete) luminary (in every sense, including lightning, happiness, etc.)
a vehicle; by implication, a team; by extension, cavalry; by analogy a rider, i.e. the upper millstone
figuratively, to trust, be confident or sure
a sister (used very widely (like brother), literally and figuratively)
